name: The Great Bestsellers: Books Millions Have Read
description: From scriptures copied for centuries to wizard schools and hobbit holes: the books that reached more readers than any others, and why they kept selling.

checkpoints.name: Old favourites
checkpoints.note: Scripture, Arabian tales, one Spanish knight and an English pilgrim's allegory: books copied by hand and then printed for centuries, read aloud in homes and temples long before anyone counted sales.

checkpoints.name: The age of the novel
checkpoints.note: Cheap printing, new schools and railway bookstalls made reading a mass habit. Fairy tales, Dickens, Wonderland, Uncle Tom's Cabin and War and Peace found readers in the millions.

checkpoints.name: The paperback century
checkpoints.note: Two world wars and the arrival of the paperback put books in soldiers' pockets and children's hands, from Christie's island murders to Tolkien's Middle-earth.

checkpoints.name: Global bestsellers
checkpoints.note: Translation, film and the internet turned some books into worldwide events, from Mao's little red book to Harry Potter and Dan Brown's thriller.
